doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Haggart and Bauduc and 'The Big Noise' at the Black Hawk
summary: Rowe asks about Haggart and Bauduc; Sherman tells how 'The Big Noise' came from improvising at Black Hawk matinees.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Was the Bob Crosby band with Bob Haggart at that time?
That’s right. That’s where they wrote “The Big Noise” from Black Hawk.
That’s right. They had matinees — well they told the story so often.

They had matinees either Saturdays or Sundays where the college kids used to come down and – I’ve forgot the whole story — but they just started improvising something, just the two of them once. And that made history.
That’s great. I know he just recently, well in the last couple of years, re-recorded that tune, without the whistling. I think he had a guitar player. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
Yeah I think I heard that.
Well yes, it’s a great tune you know, do it a lot of different ways.
